title: Shopping around
goals: Name clothes and describe what you are wearing.
Point at things that are near or far with this, that, these, those.
Understand prices and numbers in shopping conversations.
Describe gadgets with adjectives such as compact, versatile, powerful.

Join ideas with and, but, or and write a short recommendation for a product.

learn.title: this, that, these, those
learn.html:
We use them to point at things. They depend on the distance (near or far from the speaker) and on the number (one or more than one).

Near the speakerFar from the speaker
Singularthis T-shirtthat T-shirt
Pluralthese shorts / jeansthose shorts / jeans
  • Jeans, pants, shorts, shoes, socks are plural: these jeans, not this jeans. For one item: a pair of jeans.
  • They can be used alone: I like this. Those are nice.
  • This is… and That's… are used to introduce things: This is my new phone.

watch.why: The demonstrative agrees in number with the noun.

learn.title: Listening: numbers and prices
learn.html:
When you hear prices, listen to the numbers and how they are said.

WrittenSaid as
$49.95forty-nine ninety-five
$112a hundred and twelve dollars
$3.50three fifty
$250two hundred (and) fifty dollars
$1000one thousand dollars

Be careful with similar pairs: thirteen / thirty, fourteen / forty (the stress falls on different syllables).

learn.title: Comparative adjectives
learn.html:
We use them to compare two things or people: A is more ___ than B. They do not change for singular or plural.

Form: noun + be + comparative + than + noun.

RuleAdjective → Comparative
One syllable: + -ersmall → smaller, cheap → cheaper, old → older, slow → slower
Ends in -e: + -rnice → nicer, large → larger
Consonant-vowel-consonant: double the consonantbig → bigger, hot → hotter
Two syllables ending in -y: y → -ierhappy → happier, pretty → prettier, easy → easier, heavy → heavier
Long adjectives: more / less + adjectivemore compact, more up-to-date, less user-friendly, more expensive
Irregulargood → better, bad → worse
  • Less is the opposite of more: less expensive = not as expensive.
  • With than, we can use possessives: His desk is smaller than yours.

watch.wrong: This computer is more better than that one.
watch.right: This computer is better than that one.
watch.why: Better is already comparative: do not add more.

watch.wrong: My phone is more cheap than yours.
watch.right: My phone is cheaper than yours.

watch.why: The comparison word is than, not that.
Big is short: double the g and add -er.

learn.title: Compound sentences: and, but, or
learn.html:
We use them to join two ideas into one sentence.

WordFunctionExample
andadds a similar ideaThe laptop is versatile and powerful.
butcontrastsIt's not compact, but it's easy to use.
orgives a choiceYou can call or send a text message.

We put a comma before but when it joins two full sentences. Each sentence needs a subject: …but it is a little expensive.

watch.why: The subject it is missing after because.

words.en: You can choose a … or a …
words.example: You can choose a black or a grey phone.
Sometimes I get the wrong size online.
I save money when I shop online.
I don't like to hurry when I shop.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• It comes with a charger. — say what a product includes.
  • You can choose a … or a … — give options.
  • I like …, but I don't like … because … — a review with pros and cons.
  • I don't know about … — say you are not sure about something in the product.
  • I'd definitely recommend it! — end a positive review.
  • Which one is cheaper / better? — compare two options when you shop.
  • This one is more expensive than that one. — compare in the store.
  • I like these jeans. / I don't like that color. — give your opinion about clothes.

write.prompt: Choose a product you use (phone, computer, headphones…) and write a recommendation of 5 to 7 sentences: It is … and …; I like …, but …; I don't like … because …; It comes with …; I'd definitely recommend it. Include at least one comparative (It is cheaper than…).
checklist: A subject in each sentence (it is…, not is…)
At least one correct comparative with than
Better / worse when you compare with good / bad (never more better)
more / less only with long adjectives
It comes with… and I'd definitely recommend it
write.model: I use my phone every day. It is small and light, and the design is awesome. It isn't expensive, and it is cheaper than my old phone. I like the camera because it is better than my old camera. I don't like the screen because it is small. It comes with a case and a charger. I'd definitely recommend it.

write.prompt: Write a 6-line dialogue in a clothing store: ask about one item nearby and another far away (this / those), compare two, and decide which one you buy.

One comparative (This one is cheaper than that one.)
How much is / are…? to ask the price

reading.title: Two phones, two opinions
reading.intro: Read the two reviews and answer.
paragraphs: Which phone is better for you: the Zeta One or the Nova Mini? Two customers give their opinions.

Laura: I love my Zeta One. It is bigger than my old phone, and the screen is beautiful. It is more powerful than the Nova Mini, so the games are faster. It comes with a charger and headphones. But it is heavier and more expensive. It costs $450. I'd definitely recommend it for people who play games.

Mateo: I prefer the Nova Mini. It is smaller and lighter than the Zeta One, so it is more compact and fits in my pocket. It is also cheaper: only $280. It is easy to use and the battery is good. I don't like the camera because it is not very good. You can choose a black or a white phone. It is a good choice for students who need a simple phone.
Our opinion: both phones are good. The Zeta One is better for games. The Nova Mini is better if you want to save money.

listening.title: Buying sneakers
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation in the store. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'm looking for sneakers. How much are these white sneakers?
Hmm, that's a lot. And what about those black ones over there?
The black ones are fifty-four ninety-five. They're cheaper than the white ones, but the white ones are more comfortable.
Can I try the black ones? I'm a size nine.
Of course. Here you are. How are they?
They're a little big. Do you have a smaller size?
Yes, here is a size eight. Today you get a free pair of socks too.
Great, they're perfect. I'll take the black ones, please. Can I pay by card?
Yes, of course. That's fifty-four ninety-five, please.
